claim_verdicts.evidence: Sidecar Containers: "Feature state: Stable since Kubernetes v1.33"; "If an init container is created with its restartPolicy set to Always, it will start and remain running during the entire life of the Pod." Pod Lifecycle: "Sidecar containers are init containers that always restart regardless of the Pod's restartPolicy because they have their own container-level restartPolicy: Always". Docs root is current, not a 1.34 snapshot; GA since 1.33 covers 1.34.

Sidecar Containers: started status "becomes true because there is a process running in the container and no startup probe defined, or as a result of its startupProbe succeeding." Pod Lifecycle > Startup probe: "This type of probe is only executed at startup, unlike liveness and readiness probes, which are run periodically." Supports the round-2 wording "a probe the kubelet runs only while the container starts".

Init Containers: "Init containers always run to completion." "Each init container must complete successfully before the next one starts." "Init containers run to completion sequentially, and the main container does not start until all the init containers have successfully completed."

Pod Lifecycle: "the kubelet will delay sending the TERM signal to these sidecar containers until the last main container has fully terminated. The sidecar containers will be terminated in the reverse order they are defined in the Pod spec." Sidecar Containers: "Upon Pod termination, the kubelet postpones terminating sidecar containers until the main application container has fully stopped."

Pods > Pod networking: "Every container in a Pod shares the network namespace, including the IP address and network ports. Inside a Pod (and only then), the containers that belong to the Pod can communicate with one another using localhost." Execution: capture line 20-21 shows the app reaching its sidecar on 127.0.0.1:9000.

bind: "Overrides the interface to which the server's socket should bind." respond: "Writes a hard-coded/static response to the client." Concepts shorthand table: {header.*} -> {http.request.header.*}; {tls_client_subject} -> {http.request.tls.client.subject}. reverse_proxy: header_up "sets, adds..., deletes... a request header going upstream". Placeholder in respond body confirmed by execution: capture line 21 "echo app, plain HTTP, called by CN=gateway-client".

Round 2: text now names Caddy 2.10. reverse_proxy: Caddy "passes through incoming headers-including Host-to the backend without modifications"; "Since Caddy v2.11.0, this is done automatically, so it is no longer necessary to explicitly override the Host header when proxying to HTTPS." So for 2.10 Host passes unchanged. Concepts: {upstream_hostport} -> {http.reverse_proxy.upstream.hostport}. tls_client_auth, tls_trust_pool as claimed.

Global options, strict_sni_host: "Enabling this requires that a request's Host header matches the value of the ServerName"; "This option will automatically be turned on if client authentication is configured."; "HTTP status 421 Misdirected Request response is written to the client." reverse_proxy tls_server_name: "By default, this will use the upstream address' host part." 421 without header_up Host recorded from the repo run in DECISIONS.md (2026-10-26).
